Implementation of format auto-fix for story paths (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE): - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - File header and function comments reference Story 008.0 and: - `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT` - `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE` - `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE`. - getFixedStoryPath(original: string): - Guards against unsafe paths: `if (original.includes("..")) return null;` (no traversal). - No-op when already `.story.md`. - `.story` → `.story.md`. - `.md` → `.story.md`. - No extension → `.story.md` appended. - Returns null when no safe fix exists. - reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(context, comment, collapsed, fixed): - Uses context.getSourceCode().getText(comment) and searches for "@story". - Derives the exact substring containing the path value and builds a precise fix range: - `fixRange: [start + valueStartInComment, start + valueEndInComment]`. - Calls `fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed);` within context.report. - If tag or value cannot be located safely, falls back to reportInvalidStoryFormat (no fix). - validateStoryAnnotation: - Valid path regex: `^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$`. - If the original value fails but getFixedStoryPath(...) returns a string that passes this regex, it invokes reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix (so ESLint --fix will adjust only the suffix). - If no safe fix exists or there is whitespace issues, it reports invalidStoryFormat without providing a fix. - These behaviors are confirmed by tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts and tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts, which assert the corrected outputs and ensure non-fixable cases only produce errors.

traceability.notes: The story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX defines limited, safe auto-fix capabilities for missing @story annotations on functions/methods and for simple @story path suffix normalization. Those capabilities are fully implemented in the ESLint rules `require-story-annotation` and `valid-annotation-format`, which declare `meta.fixable: "code"` and use ESLint fixer APIs to insert a placeholder @story template or adjust `.story`/`.md` suffixes only. The helpers in src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts and src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts ensure changes are minimal, avoid modifying runtime behavior, and skip potentially unsafe cases (e.g., paths with traversal). Behavior is thoroughly covered by tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts and the per-rule test files, which validate before/after code for both missing-annotation and path-format scenarios, including TS-specific constructs and non-fixable error cases. user-docs/api-reference.md documents exactly what `--fix` does for these rules, including current limitations and safety constraints, matching the story’s acceptance criteria for documentation. REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE are explicitly marked in the story as not yet implemented and scoped to future work, and the current implementation aligns with the “Current Auto-Fix Capabilities (This Iteration)” described in the spec. Given the concrete rule implementations, targeted tests tied directly to docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md, and accurate user-facing documentation, all in-scope acceptance criteria for this story are satisfied, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
